Fwiw I think this language change was more "good housekeeping" than forward guidance of imminent coupo auction cuts. Of course anything is possible and for instance increasing bills percentage would be dovish/debasing. Realistically the debt and deficit is growing rapidly and they will have to issue more of everything.  However from a housekeeping standpoint and in preparation for any balance sheet changes from the Fed I prefer changes 

On housekeeping 
they could kill the 20 year for example or reduce SFR's or a tips auction sizes for no particular reason or for an idiosyncratic reason

On Fed if Fed changes reinvestment policy to say less 10's and more 2's on add ons treasury may want to partly respond to that by cutting private sector 2's and increasing 10's. 

Of course the Fed could once again do sizable RMP's (though zero this month) which would in fact be dovish/debase because that would cause less financing need and less of all auctions. Or they could cut balance sheet and cause increases.

Simply put.  Treasury financing needs is going up rapidly and they will have to sell more of everything.  The language change is good housekeeping for tweaks and good prep for Fed balance sheet changes. 

If gold and stocks reacted to this news which they may have it was likely an overreaction.

A low revenue multiple tells you less about how cheap a protocol is than how much confidence the market has in its revenue.  

xRev compares a protocol’s market cap with its annualized revenue. Direction alone can be misleading.   

A falling xRev may reflect revenue growth that valuation has not caught up with. It may also mean market cap is falling faster than revenue.   

A rising xRev may reflect valuation moving higher or revenue declining faster than market cap.  

Comparing trailing xRev with the current run rate clarifies what is happening on the revenue side. The trailing multiple can remain low because it still includes stronger revenue months that have already passed.   

The latest 30-day pace shows whether that multiple reflects what the protocol is earning today.  Revenue that proves durable can change market expectations.

Here’s why he matters to this prize specifically:
Neal wrote the argument Future Vision XPRIZE is built on: that science fiction stopped handing engineers something to build and started handing them only warnings.

Stephenson’s The Diamond Age (1995) is about an AI tutor that raises a child. 31 years later it's become the entire goal of AI education history. While he did not predict this outcome, he provided the blueprints to make it possible.

Out of one book real products were made by real engineers

Think about that, a word he made up was capable of reorganizing trillion-dollar companies.

The Future Vision XPRIZE finals will be hosted at Moonshots LIVE on Sep 25th in Los Angeles.

We’re asking filmmakers to do in three minutes what he’s done in novels for thirty years: describe a future so specific and so compelling that someone goes out and builds it.

He is exactly the right person to judge whether they pulled it off.

Rather than critiquing the problem, he founded Project Hieroglyph at Arizona State. Built on creating stories that inspire construction instead of fear. That’s the entire thesis of this prize.

here’s the best advice I’ve ever received:

“you need to stop thinking about it as money, and start thinking about it as time.”

please take 2 mins to read this because that bit of advice will dramatically change your quality of life.

it sounds silly when you start to think: 

“how much time am I spending to buy this?” instead of “how much money?”

but I’ll tell you why it’s not with the following example: 

the average car payment a month is £400 ($540) over a 5 year period.

the average car payment a month is 1 weeks worth of wages after tax a month.

the average person is trading 1/4 of their time every single month to drive a car.

how much would you pay to add an extra week to every single month? 

imagine the freedom you would have?

so why do we sell that time for £400?

because in doing so you’re selling the experiences and moments that might have been.

> time with your family
> time with your hobbies 
> time to learn something new
> time to focus on your health

you forego all of that when you sign that contract for a cheap dopamine hit for that new hot car with all the extra trimmings.

so start asking yourself “how much time am I spending to buy this?” from now on.

there’s other benefits that come from this as you liberate yourself from the burden of materialistic possession’s.

the things that you own will end up owning you. (bookmark it) 👇

1. A good writer isn't someone elaborate, or sophisticated. It's someone who can explain concepts simply, and someone you simply enjoy reading

I think most software will be created by AI, and increasingly most software will also be consumed by AI on our behalf. So we’re going to see an explosion of software, not a reduction.

Looking at my own usage, I estimate that:

• For every web search I do, AI does 1,000x more
• For every email I send, AI sends 100x more
• For every SMS I send, AI sends 10x more
• For every spreadsheet I open, AI probably queries/manipulates 1000x more data behind the scenes

The conclusion is pretty simple: we should start building software for agents, because agents are going to become the primary users.
